blocking.title: Index.append ignores short writes (cps_vm.py:690), so INDEX events such as a START can vanish on a full tmpfs
blocking.why_blocking: Confirmed major on two integrity paths. A lost START record leads next_attempt to write a second START for the same attempt, which is a hidden retry. Lost made, verified or evicted records corrupt the bounded-retry and verification bookkeeping, which is evidence integrity.

conditions_before_release: Fix every blocking item. Each fix needs a regression test that fails on HEAD 95df270: wipe before the AI-V1r2 upload (F1); two STARTs for one attempt (F2, OP-01, TST-01); a pending stage needing an FZ download at restore (F3); a reset-caused second interruption and a technically failed run without output (F4, FLAGS-3); audit run on a listing that contains an incident the final listing missed (F5); an unreadable folder or special-mode file before evict (SAFE-01); a short INDEX write (SAFE-04); a wrong or real-carrier --empty-carrier (FLAGS-1); a placeholder conversation id (OP-04); a lost INCIDENT upload at recheck (OP-02); a truncated ALL_FROZEN.json (OP-03); an invalid --case (SAFE-02); probe-p5 start and check run in one call (SAFE-03).

Obtain a new admission review of the fixed candidate under a new version id. Review the diff against 95df270 plus the restore, incident, save-point, final and audit core in full. Re-run the mutation set M08, M10, M14, M16, M19, M24, M26, M27, M30-M32, M34, M37 and M39 on a machine with enough disk, and require every mutant to be killed.

Get one green full run of test_cps_vm.py, all scenarios in a single run, on a machine with at least about 1 GB free. Record the actual test count and reconcile it with README.md:268 (which claims 1,678; this review counted 1,595 because of ENOSPC truncation). Also require test_make_kit.py 19/19.

Answer probes P1-P5 and record them. P5 must use the fixed probe-p5, which records the caller's ppid and session id and refuses a same-call check. P2 must establish whether the connector can save a full listing to a VM file verbatim; this settles OP-06. Also measure the cold setup duration against the platform's tool-call limit (SAFE-07).
Get the owner's decision on transcript export and upload for conversations that wrote and were lost (F7) before qualification starts.
Admit the pre-gate separately before any release names it.
Correct the Drive-call budget in the README and spec (OP-07: about 29 Drive calls per normal run) so that owner time planning and P2 sizing use real numbers.
The 38 reserved answers stay closed. No fix may need them, and the frozen evaluator, the aggregator e5aa4fc7 and runner v4 7505e98a stay unchanged.

simplification_advice:
Yes, the size is a risk in itself, and these results show it. The rule-breaking findings (F1, F2, F3, OP-01, SAFE-04, F5) are not exotic. Each is a seam where one of about 19 subcommands carries its own copy of a state rule: whether a save point is confirmed, whether a conversation is open, which stage is pending, which runs failed. 7.5k lines of helper plus 4.8k lines of tests produce more distinct printed situations than an LLM operator, or one review round, can reliably cover. Each extra branch is one more place where the Dot can follow a printed line into a hidden retry. Simplifications that keep every rule:
(1) One save-point primitive. Every note and package (START, LINK, AI, INCIDENT, CP, FZ, LEDGER_FINAL, ALL_FROZEN) goes through the same sequence: upload, narrow listing, md5 confirm, bounded re-upload, then STOP. Nothing that depends on a note being on Drive may print the next step until the note is confirmed. This alone closes OP-01, OP-02, OP-03 and OP-08, and most of F2.
(2) One open-conversation rule for every AI role, continuations included. When an AI role has a START, or a REVIEW_INCOMPLETE continuation, newer than its newest confirmed archive, the only path is confirm-ended, then export the transcript, then choose: NOTHING_WRITTEN (one restart) or WRITTEN (failed, upload the transcript). Remove the special 'archived' and continuation branches. This closes F1 and F7 and simplifies incident_plan.
(3) Derive the failure flags in one pure function, from the notes plus the frozen records, and call it from both final and audit, with audit running it on its own listing and reporting any difference. Have apply_frozen_flags take the empty-carrier files and compute the carrier hashes itself. That closes F4, F5, FLAGS-1, FLAGS-2 and FLAGS-3 with less code than today.
(4) Make restore classification fail closed. Any state the classifier cannot settle without a download (F3), or any listing that is not provably complete, prints the downloads and asks again. It never falls back to NONE_IN_FLIGHT.
(5) Replace full-folder hand-saved listings with name-prefix queries for the current job plus one bounded 'newer than the last SESSION' listing (OP-06), or prove with P2 that the connector writes listings to a file.
(6) Split everyday and qualification into separate entry modules over a shared core. Drop or quarantine probe-p5 and other one-off tooling from the operator command set. Keep the operator's surface to essentially 'run status, then run exactly the printed line', with every attested value validated against a strict pattern (no {TOKEN}, no space in the case id).
(7) Enforce tests mechanically. A lint test should fail if any refuse or stop code in cps_vm.py never appears in test_cps_vm.py. That would have caught TST-01..TST-07.
(8) Use durable primitives: write INDEX with a full-write loop and fsync (SAFE-04), walk trees with onerror=raise (SAFE-01). Each change is a few lines and removes a whole class of silent loss.
For the next admission round, review the diff of the fixed core rather than the whole 7.5k lines, so the review stays tractable.
rationale: The rules say any confirmed or plausible critical, or any confirmed major on an integrity rule, blocks admission. F1 is a confirmed critical, verified by an independent re-run: a reviewer revision that was written and then lost to a reset is classified AI_ARCHIVED, and the same reviewer is prompted again. That is a hidden retry under O46, it can turn FAIL into PASS, and nothing flags it. That alone decides DO_NOT_ADMIT. Several confirmed majors also sit on integrity rules. On no hidden retry: F2, OP-01, SAFE-04, and TST-01 (a missing test on a hidden-retry guard). On O44: F3, an unbound re-run of a stage lost to a reset. On O46 failure recording: F4 and F5. On evidence loss: SAFE-01. On freeze immutability and wrong scores: OP-04 and FLAGS-1. Further majors are not integrity rules but still exclude ADMIT_WITH_CONDITIONS, which allows only minor items and conditions outside the code: OP-02, OP-03, SAFE-02, SAFE-03, FLAGS-3, and the plausible OP-06. Both scopes are refused because everyday shares the faulty core and has its own wedge (SAFE-02). The verifiers downgraded F2 to major, OP-05 to minor and KIT-1 to minor. I took those downgrades into account and they do not change the outcome. I keep SAFE-03 as major even though its twin OP-05 was downgraded, because it falsifies the evidence for a release gate. What the reviews found sound: archive extraction safety, kit sha pinning and make_kit --expect, the lock handed to the detached worker, refusal of a second restart, A-before-B (backed by runner v4, which stays unchanged), protection of frozen folders by verify-frozen, the ledger and fork checks at final and audit, and no exposure of reserved answers. The fixes are mostly local, and a re-admission is realistic after the simplifications above.
